topic_tag: the first recording of a ballad
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: One folklorist has argued that the 1928 recording had ______ the ballad.

worlds.passage: In 1928 a record company made the first recording of an old ballad from the hill counties, about a ferryman drowned in a flood. Before then, collectors had written down more than thirty versions of it across the hill counties, with different verses, tunes, and endings. The record sold in every county store. When collectors returned to the same counties in the 1950s, a single notebook page held what their predecessors had needed thirty for, and some older singers apologized that their grandmothers had sung it wrong. One folklorist has argued that the 1928 recording had ______ the ballad.
worlds.explanation: Thirty-odd local versions before the record, a single page's worth afterward, and singers calling their grandmothers' versions wrong combine to show the record's version replaced the others, so the recording "standardized" the ballad. "Sweetened" fails because what changed was how many versions survived, not how pleasant the song sounded. "Secularized" fails because nothing in the passage concerns a religious use of the ballad. "Unearthed" fails because the ballad was already widely sung.

sweetened.why: the change was in how many versions survived, not toward a smoother sound

secularized.quote: with different verses, tunes, and endings
secularized.why: the variety that disappeared was local variation, not sacred use

unearthed.why: the ballad was well known before the record, so it was not rediscovered

worlds.passage: In 1928 a record company made the first recording of an old ballad from the hill counties, about a ferryman drowned in a flood. In the hill counties singers had always performed it without accompaniment, in a hard, nasal voice. On the record a studio orchestra played softly under a tenor trained for the concert hall, who sang every verse slowly and smoothly. City reviewers, few of whom had ever heard the hill versions sung, praised how much easier on the ear the old song had become. One folklorist has argued that the 1928 recording had ______ the ballad.
worlds.explanation: The record replaced the hill singers' harsh, bare sound with a soft orchestra and a smooth trained voice, and city listeners found it easier on the ear; combining the old sound with the new shows the recording "sweetened" the ballad. "Standardized" fails because the passage concerns the ballad's sound, not whether its many versions became one. "Secularized" fails because nothing sacred was removed; every verse was kept and only the sound changed. "Unearthed" fails because the ballad was already sung throughout the hill counties.

standardized.quote: a studio orchestra played softly under a tenor
standardized.why: the record changed the ballad's sound, not the number of versions people sang

secularized.quote: sang every verse slowly and smoothly
secularized.why: the words were kept whole; the change was to the sound

unearthed.why: the ballad was a living song before the record, not a lost one

worlds.passage: In 1928 a record company made the first recording of an old ballad from the hill counties, about a ferryman drowned in a flood. In the hill counties it had been sung only in church at funerals, and its last verse was a prayer for the ferryman's soul. The record kept the hill singers' hard voices and fiddle, replaced the prayer with a verse naming the river and the year of the flood, and was sold to the dance halls, where it was played between reels. One folklorist has argued that the 1928 recording had ______ the ballad.
worlds.explanation: The record took a funeral hymn, removed its prayer, and sent it to the dance halls, so the recording "secularized" the ballad. "Standardized" fails because the passage concerns where and why the ballad was sung, not the number of versions. "Sweetened" fails because the record kept the hill singers' hard sound. "Unearthed" fails because the ballad was already sung at every funeral in the hill counties.

standardized.quote: sung only in church at funerals
standardized.why: the change was from sacred to worldly use, not from many versions to one

sweetened.quote: kept the hill singers' hard voices

unearthed.quote: its last verse was a prayer
unearthed.why: the ballad had an established place in church life, so it was not lost

worlds.passage: In 1928 a record company made the first recording of an old ballad from the hill counties, about a ferryman drowned in a flood. No collector in the hill counties had found it before 1928. The singer on the record had learned it as a child from an aunt, the last person in her valley who knew it, and sang every verse to the aunt's tune in the aunt's hard, plain style. After the record appeared, folklorists traced its verses to a broadside printed in 1790 and added it to their collections. One folklorist has argued that the 1928 recording had ______ the ballad.
worlds.explanation: A ballad no collector had found, kept alive by one old woman, was recorded as she sang it, and only then did scholars trace and collect it; combining these shows the record brought a lost song to light, so the recording "unearthed" the ballad. "Standardized" fails because only one version survived, so there was nothing to make uniform. "Sweetened" fails because the singer kept the aunt's hard, plain style. "Secularized" fails because the record sang every verse as the aunt had.

standardized.quote: the last person in her valley who knew it
standardized.why: a single surviving version leaves nothing to make uniform

sweetened.why: the singer kept the old sound

secularized.quote: sang every verse to the aunt's tune
secularized.why: the record kept the ballad's verses whole, so nothing sacred was taken out
